name: Language exam preparation
description: Level up a language and pass an official exam (IELTS, TOEFL, DELE, DELF, Goethe, JLPT...). Covers the four skills, vocabulary, grammar and timed mock exams, and ends with an exam week.

steps.title: Diagnose your level and choose the exam
steps.description: Take a free placement test, read the exam format and scoring, and decide the exam date and the score you need.

steps.title: Set up your study system
steps.description: Choose a course book, an app and a notebook, plan a weekly timetable and create your vocabulary deck.

steps.title: Core grammar review
steps.description: Revise the structures the exam relies on: tenses, conditionals, connectors, reported speech. Do exercises after each topic.

steps.title: Vocabulary: the first 1,000 words
steps.description: Learn high-frequency and exam-topic words in context, with example sentences, and review them daily with flashcards.

steps.title: Listening skills
steps.description: Train with exam-style recordings: predict answers, catch synonyms, practise note-taking and dictation.

steps.title: Reading skills
steps.description: Practise skimming, scanning and inference on exam texts. Time every exercise and review each wrong answer.

steps.title: Writing skills
steps.description: Learn the structure of each task type, write one text a week and get it corrected or compare it with model answers.

steps.title: Speaking skills
steps.description: Record yourself answering exam questions, shadow native speakers and practise with a partner or tutor.

steps.title: Timed mock exam 1 and error analysis
steps.description: Sit a full mock exam in real conditions, then sort every mistake by cause: knowledge, timing or carelessness.

steps.title: Targeted weak-spot training
steps.description: Spend the time where the mock exam showed the biggest losses instead of what feels comfortable.

steps.title: Timed mock exams 2 and 3
steps.description: Two more full mock exams, a week apart, with the same analysis. Aim for a margin above the score you need.

steps.title: Exam week: logistics and light review
steps.description: Check documents, route and rules, sleep well and only review summaries and flashcards.

competencies.name: Listening
competencies.description: Understand recordings at exam speed and pick out the detail the questions ask for.

competencies.name: Reading
competencies.description: Read exam texts within the time limit and answer inference questions.

competencies.name: Writing
competencies.description: Write clear, well-organised texts of the required type and length with few errors.

competencies.name: Speaking
competencies.description: Answer spontaneously, develop ideas with examples and be easy to understand.

competencies.name: Vocabulary and grammar
competencies.description: Range and accuracy of the words and structures you can use without thinking.

cards.front: CEFR A1 and A2: what can you do?
cards.back: Basic user: understand and use everyday expressions, introduce yourself and ask and answer simple questions on familiar topics.

cards.front: CEFR B1: what can you do?
cards.back: Independent user: deal with most travel situations, describe experiences and plans, and give brief reasons and opinions.

cards.front: CEFR B2: what can you do?
cards.back: Understand the main ideas of complex texts, interact with native speakers without strain and write clear, detailed text.

cards.front: CEFR C1: what can you do?
cards.back: Proficient user: understand demanding long texts, express ideas fluently and spontaneously and use the language flexibly for work and study.

cards.front: CEFR C2: what can you do?
cards.back: Understand virtually everything heard or read, summarise information from several sources and express yourself precisely, with fine shades of meaning.

cards.front: How do you approach a listening task with questions?
cards.back: Read the questions first, predict the type of answer, listen for synonyms of the question words and never leave an answer blank.

cards.front: How should you use the first minutes of a writing task?
cards.back: Plan for about five minutes: position, two arguments with examples, conclusion. Keep the last few minutes to check grammar, spelling and word count.

cards.front: What do examiners reward in the speaking test?
cards.back: Fluency and coherence, range of vocabulary, range and accuracy of grammar, and pronunciation. Extend answers with reasons and examples.

cards.front: Why do timed mock exams matter?
cards.back: They train timing, stamina and technique. Review every mistake and write down the rule behind it.
